name: SendPulse subscription for WooCommerce
author: SendPulse

sections.description:
SendPulse email subscription plugin for WooCommerce lets you transfer email, name, phone number, company, city, state, and country of your WooCommerce customers to SendPulse automatically.

Go to SendPulse website, sign up for a free account and enable API. Unlike other email marketing services SendPulse offers free autoresponders and free web push notifications.

So when your customer creates an order or an order is completed you can start email marketing to them using autoresponder emails. Set up your thank-you email, feedback requests, upsells and more and SendPulse will send them to all your customers at the right time.

FEATURES

  • Install the plugin in 1 click and set up within minutes;
  • Set up autoresponder for transactional emails;
  • Let customers subscribe to marketing emails with an opt-in checkbox.

SENDPULSE’S KEY FEATURES

  • Rich automation possibilities that allow you to create email, SMS, web push, and chatbot campaigns on one platform;
  • Drag and drop email editor;
  • Ready-made email templates;
  • Email personalization and list segmentation;
  • Detailed analytics and reports.

WHAT IS SENDPULSE?

SendPulse is a multi-channel marketing automation platform for multifaceted business promotion and customer retention.

SendPulse allows you to send email, SMS, and web push campaigns, stay in touch with clients using Telegram, Facebook Messenger, WhatsApp, and Instagram chatbots, and create landing pages in just 15 minutes.

You can easily track all of your marketing activities and gather customer data with SendPulse’s free CRM.

Create a SendPulse account, and send up to 15,000 emails every month for free.

You can install SendPulse Free WebPush plugin if you need a plugin for web push notifications or add subscription forms on your WordPress website with SendPulse Email Marketing Newsletter plugin.

Guide for the WooCommerce plugin is available in the SendPulse knowledge base.

External Services

This plugin connects to the SendPulse API to enable its functionality, such as managing email campaigns, creating mailing lists, and sending notifications. By using this plugin, you agree to the terms and policies of SendPulse Inc, as the plugin relies on their external services.

For more information about SendPulse Inc services, please refer to the following:

  • SendPulse Terms of Use
  • SendPulse Privacy Policy
  • SendPulse Security

Using this plugin implies consent to interact with the SendPulse API and the data transfer required for its features. Please review the above links to ensure you are comfortable with our policies.

Contacts

  • Customer support – https://sendpulse.com/support
  • Twitter – https://twitter.com/SendPulseCom
  • Facebook – https://facebook.com/sendpulse
sections.installation:
Installation is plain and simple

  1. Add the plugin to WordPress by searching and installing, uploading a zip, FTP copy, or some other way, and activate it
  2. Mark the checkbox in the settings to turn it on.
  3. Get your API Key and Secret from SendPulse. You must be registered and logged into your account.
  4. Paste your Api Key and Api Secret into Plugin Settings Page: WooCommerce -> Settings -> Integration -> Integration WooCommerce SendPulse
  5. Select “Keep token at” dropdown field into desired position. Recommended: Database
  6. Select event to fire subscribe at “Subscribe Event” dropdown field
  7. Select checkbox at “Enable WooCommerce SendPulse”
  8. Click “Save changes”
  9. Select desired mailing list from dropdown at “Mailing list” option.
  10. Click “Save changes”

Optional:
1. Use “Display an Opt-In Field on Checkout”
2. Set “Opt-In Field Label” you want
3. Choose “Opt-In Checkbox Default Status”
4. Choose “Opt-In Checkbox Display Location”

Debug:
1. Check “Check to enable Debug Mode” checkbox
2. Edit wp-config.php and set WP_DEBUG and WP_DEBUG_LOG to “true”
3. Look for problems at wp-content/debug.log file

IMPORTANT: Do NOT keep debug enabled on production all the time!
After you finished debug set WP_DEBUG and WP_DEBUG_LOG to “false”.
Disable “Check to enable Debug Mode” checkbox
